findings.severity: major (incomplete fix of GAP-267; regression vs run-1 navStartedAt scoping)
findings.title: GAP-267's unscoped main-document lookup is keyed on exact equality with the FINAL page.url(), so the audited page's own 4xx/5xx is still dropped whenever the final URL differs from the response URL

repro.CLI --json (probe-cli-own404.json): own-404 6/6 reported; own-404-empty 0/6, own-500-empty 0/6, own-404-hash 0/6 (report.url is chrome-error://chromewebdata/ for the empty-body cases). Exit 0 without --fail-on-diff; exit 1 with it only because of Chrome's generic console error.

findings.cause: runtime.ts audit(): mainDocumentResponse = last network entry with resourceType==='document' && n.url === page.url(). The response was logged before the cross-document commit, so scopeToDocument drops it, and the fallback lookup can't find it because page.url() has since changed (same-document hash/replaceState) or is chrome-error://chromewebdata/. Before fix-1 (run-1's navStartedAt-based scoping) these responses were inside the scope window.
findings.mitigation_observed: Chrome's own 'Failed to load resource ... 404' console error is still in consoleErrors, so --fail-on-diff still exits 1; brokenRequests is still wrong for any machine consumer.
findings.fixDirection: identify the main document response by navigation identity (page.goto's returned HTTPResponse, or Network.responseReceived type Document for the main frame/loaderId on the dedicated CDP session), not by string equality with the post-load page.url()

findings.severity: minor (pre-existing GAP-new-E, but it defeats GAP-267 on a top real site)
findings.title: The page's own 404 is evicted from the 200-entry network ring buffer on heavy pages, so GAP-267's 'captured unscoped' claim fails there while coversWholeDocument stays true

findings.title: fix-2 awaits Page.enable on a brand-new CDPSession before every audit({url}); Chrome holds that call when the tab has an open JS dialog or an uncommitted pending navigation, stalling the audit for up to the dialog auto-dismiss (30s) or the full protocolTimeout (180s), and on the 180s path the session is never detached

repro.open alert on current page, then audit({: 3/3: 31051/31058/31060ms (Page.enable alone 29.5s) vs plain runtime.navigate to the same url 11-12ms and a normal audit ~1555ms
repro.previous navigation timed out with no re: 182s-200s+ in 5/5 occurrences (probe-hang-audit-first, probe-hang-hangcontam, probe-runtime-redirects hang_* rows); Page.enable 180003-180012ms; plain navigate in the same situation 10-30010ms
repro.CDP session leak on that path: created 67 / detached 66 in probe-runtime-redirects; probe-hang cdp records show no detach after the 180s Page.enable timeout (catch sets navCdpSession=null before finally, so detach is skipped)
repro.result correctness on the stalled path: report still correct (no GAP-262 contamination seen, probe-hang-hangcontam)

findings.cause: runtime.ts audit(): await client.send("Page.enable") on the fresh session. packages/browser/src/session/dialog-cdp.ts:425-427 already documents that a fresh Page.enable blocks for the full protocolTimeout while a dialog is open and deliberately does not await it there. fix-1 (puppeteer framenavigated) had no such call.
findings.fixDirection: do not await Page.enable unboundedly (fire-and-forget like dialog-cdp.ts, or race it with a short timeout), and detach the session in every path including the catch
